title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: exclude specific domains from web grounding
summary: The briefing passes: the domain-exclusion script, limits, default and governance controls are supported by Microsoft documentation, and the rollout facts match the roadmap. Minor corrections should complete the Purview path, put the Graph request properties in the control note, and acknowledge Microsoft's alternative Microsoft 365 E7 licensing route.

The feature lets administrators specify sites to exclude from web grounding in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: This feature will allow admins to specify a limited set of sites to exclude from web grounding in M365 Copilot and Copilot Chat #copilotcontrolsystem

claims.claim: With web search enabled, Copilot and Copilot Chat may ground responses in public web content.
claims.quote: When web search is enabled, Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat may fetch information from the Bing search service when information from the web helps to provide a better, more grounded response.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table and Graph paragraph
claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can apply the web-search setting through an applyOnce baseline.
claims.quote: Create a new configurationMonitor object that runs periodically in the background at a scheduled frequency to detect configuration drift in monitorOnly mode, or applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode.
claims.fix: Keep the call. Append to controls[1].note and the rendered note: 'Request body: mode=applyOnce; baseline.resources uses resourceType=microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch, resourceVersion=1 and properties.value as a string (0 enables, 1 disables, 2 disables Work mode only).' These properties are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-copilot-resources#allowwebsearch-resource-type and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/configurationmanagement-post-configurationmonitors?view=graph-rest-beta; they currently appear only in the prose.

claims.claim: The Graph automation is preview.
claims.quote: These capabilities are available in preview through Microsoft Graph beta.

claims.claim: TCM supports the Copilot web-search setting only in tenant-level policies.
claims.quote: TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.claim: The Graph operation fails for this resource if the setting is configured in a group-level policy.
claims.quote: Before using TCM, ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy in that admin center. If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and applyOnce fail for that resource.

claims.claim: The signed-in administrator needs the AI Administrator role for the web-search applyOnce operation.
claims.quote: For remediation and applyOnce, AI Administrator is the least-privileged Microsoft Entra role for the signed-in user. This role requirement applies to the user, not to the TCM service principal.

claims.claim: The monitor's mode for applying the desired web-search configuration once is applyOnce.
claims.quote: mode | monitorMode | The monitor mode. The possible values are: monitorOnly, applyOnce, unknownFutureValue. Optional; defaults to monitorOnly.

claims.claim: The baseline resourceType is microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch.
claims.quote: "resourceType": "microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch"

claims.claim: The baseline resourceVersion is 1.
claims.quote: "resourceVersion": 1

claims.claim: The deciding baseline property is properties.value and its value is a string.
String value 0 enables web search in Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: 0 enables it in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: String value 1 disables web search in both experiences.
claims.quote: 1 disables it in both.

claims.claim: String value 2 disables web search in Work mode while enabling it in Web mode and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: 2 disables it in Microsoft 365 Copilot Work mode while enabling it in Microsoft 365 Copilot Web mode and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.where: controls[2].governs; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Purview DLP can block external web search when Copilot prompt text matches configured sensitive information types.
claims.quote: When a user prompt contains the configured SITs, Copilot and Cowork block external web search as a grounding source and continue to generate the response using allowed internal Microsoft 365 data sources.

claims.claim: The printed Purview path reaches the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location in a Custom DLP policy.
claims.quote:
Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy.
Select the Custom template, then Custom policy.
On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.
claims.fix: Complete controls[2].ui.path and the rendered path as 'Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork > rule > Content contains > Sensitive information types > Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches'. The current path stops at the correct location rather than the web-search action. The remaining labels are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-microsoft365-copilot-location-learn-about#block-sensitive-information-types-in-web-search.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule -Policy <policy> -RestrictWebGrounding $true creates a rule in an existing DLP policy with the web-grounding block action.
claims.quote:
The Policy parameter specifies the existing DLP policy that contains the new DLP rule.
The RestrictWebGrounding parameter specifies an action for the DLP rule that blocks web grounding.
$true: Web grounding is blocked.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule and RestrictWebGrounding are documented in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote:
This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
RestrictWebGrounding
Applicable: Security & Compliance

claims.claim: The web-search blocking rule uses Content contains > Sensitive information types with the selected SITs.
claims.quote: Add a rule with the Content contains > Sensitive information types condition and choose the SITs you want to detect.

claims.claim: The rule action is Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches.
claims.quote: In the same rule, set the action to Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches.

claims.claim: The documented DLP procedure saves and turns on the policy.
claims.quote: Save and turn on the policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Domain exclusion filters incoming results rather than preventing the generated web-search query from being sent to Bing.
claims.quote: Currently, domain exclusions support filtering on web page results only.

claims.claim: Generated Bing queries consist of a few words informed by the user's prompt.
claims.quote: This generated search query is different from the user's original prompt-it consists of a few words informed by the user's prompt.

claims.claim: Generated Bing queries do not include entire Microsoft 365 files.
claims.quote:
The following information isn't included in the generated search query sent to the Bing search service:
Entire Microsoft 365 files (for example, emails or documents) or files uploaded into Copilot

claims.claim: Generated queries can be informed by organizational document content.
claims.quote:
However, it may also be informed by data within a Microsoft 365 document under the following conditions:
When a user enters a prompt into Copilot inside a Microsoft 365 application
When the user explicitly references a specific document in their prompt.

claims.claim: A generated query can use a manager's name found in Microsoft 365 data.
claims.quote: Copilot finds the name of the user's manager from Microsoft 365 data. It then generates a Bing search query based on their name to see what information about them is available on the web.

claims.claim: A very short prompt can itself form the generated search query.
claims.quote: The user's entire prompt, unless the prompt is very short (for example, "local weather")
